title: Career Roadmap: Data Analyst
summary: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyzes, and interprets data to help organizations make informed decisions. With a B.Sc. in Econometrics or Economics (Hons), graduates can specialize in economic analysis, market research, business intelligence, financial analytics, policy evaluation, and forecasting.

blocks.text: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, analyzes, and interprets data to help organizations make informed decisions. With a B.Sc. in Econometrics or Economics (Hons), graduates can specialize in economic analysis, market research, business intelligence, financial analytics, policy evaluation, and forecasting.
Collect and validate datasets, perform statistical analysis, identify trends, build dashboards, and communicate actionable findings.
Banks, consulting firms, technology companies, e-commerce businesses, research institutions, government-related projects, and economic policy organizations.
Business intelligence, economic data analysis, financial analytics, consumer insights, and quantitative research.

Prioritize programs that include statistics, econometrics, quantitative methods, and practical computing. A degree title alone does not guarantee sufficient technical preparation; review the syllabus before choosing a college.

rows.text: Understand markets, businesses, and economic indicators
Estimate relationships and test economic hypotheses
Support statistical modeling and quantitative analysis
Analyze trends, seasonality, and economic forecasts
Communicate findings through charts and dashboards

blocks.text: Learn Excel, descriptive statistics, probability, data cleaning, pivot tables, and basic charts. Practice with public economic datasets.
Practice SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries, and window functions. Learn Python with pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib.
Learn Power BI or Tableau, data modeling, calculated measures, filters, and dashboard storytelling.
Practice regression, hypothesis testing, correlation, confidence intervals, and time-series analysis. Learn to distinguish correlation from causation.
Complete three strong portfolio projects, publish clear documentation, practice case studies, and apply for internships and entry-level roles.

The timeline is a suggested sequence, not a requirement to wait a full year before applying. Students can begin applying for internships as soon as they have foundational skills and one credible project.

items.text: Pivot tables, conditional formatting, data validation
Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and Seaborn
Missing-value handling, outlier checks, grouping and merging
Statistical tests, regression and reproducible analysis
Extracting reliable datasets from relational databases
Dashboard design, KPI selection, data modeling and calculated measures
Regression, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals
R or Stata as useful additional tools for economics research
Microsoft Power BI — Microsoft Learn training

blocks.text: Employers need evidence that you can turn raw data into reliable insights. Build at least three projects, ideally including one economics-focused project.

rows.text: Compare inflation, GDP growth and interest-rate trends over time
Explore price differences across products, regions or periods
Analyze revenue, profit, product categories and monthly trends
Investigate associations between education and employment indicators
Compare simple forecasting approaches and evaluate errors

items.text: Obtain public data from the Reserve Bank of India or World Bank.
Clean dates, missing values, units, and inconsistent categories.
Use Python or Excel to calculate percentage changes and summary statistics.
Build a Power BI dashboard showing trends and comparisons.
Write a short report explaining the main findings, limitations, and possible explanations.
Publish the code, dashboard screenshots, and report in a GitHub repository.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: describe observed relationships accurately. A dashboard showing two variables moving together does not establish that one caused the other.

Search for roles that match your current skills. A student with Excel and Power BI may start in reporting or business intelligence, while a student with strong SQL, Python, and statistics can target more technical analyst roles.

Certifications can structure learning, but they do not replace practical projects or demonstrated skills.

blocks.label: Suggested order
blocks.text: start with Excel and SQL, add Python, then learn Power BI. Pursue a certification once you can complete practical exercises independently.

A postgraduate qualification can be valuable for candidates aiming at advanced statistical analysis, economic research, forecasting, or quantitative finance. It is not always necessary for entry-level Data Analyst positions.

Before applying, check mathematics prerequisites, entrance examinations, and whether the program includes programming and applied projects. Some data science programs require stronger mathematics or computing backgrounds.
Data Analyst Intern, Junior Data Analyst, Reporting Analyst, MIS Analyst.

blocks.text: Excel, SQL, data cleaning, basic statistics, dashboards, and clear reporting.
Business Intelligence Analyst, Senior Data Analyst, Economic Analyst, Product Analyst.

Analytics Consultant, Analytics Manager, Data Scientist, Econometrician, Quantitative Researcher.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: advanced modeling, strategic decisions, domain specialization, mentoring, and team leadership.
Progression depends on demonstrated skills, work experience, business knowledge, and role requirements—not simply years of service.

blocks.label: AI-assisted analytics
blocks.text: use AI tools to help draft SQL queries, explain code, and explore datasets. Verify outputs before relying on them.

blocks.label: Automated reporting
blocks.text: create repeatable data pipelines and scheduled dashboards.

blocks.label: Cloud data platforms
blocks.text: gain introductory exposure to tools such as BigQuery or Microsoft Fabric.

blocks.label: Predictive analytics
blocks.text: learn forecasting and regression before moving to complex machine learning.

blocks.label: Data governance and privacy
blocks.text: understand data quality, access control, confidentiality, and responsible data use.
For an economics graduate, combining econometrics + SQL + Python + Power BI is a particularly practical way to stand out from candidates who know only dashboard tools.
Use this checklist to track progress. The plan assumes a three-year undergraduate degree; adapt it if the program has a different duration.
Study probability, statistics, and introductory economics
Learn SQL, joins, aggregations, and window functions
Build a Power BI or Tableau dashboard
Practice SQL interviews and analytical case studies
Prepare a resume and portfolio repository
Apply for internships and entry-level analyst roles
For a student pursuing B.Sc. Econometrics / Economics (Hons), the strongest route into data analytics is:

items.text: Build a solid foundation in statistics, economics, and Excel.
Learn SQL for querying data and Python for cleaning and analysis.
Add Power BI or Tableau for visualization and reporting.
Use econometrics to develop a specialization in economic, financial, or market analysis.
Complete three portfolio projects using credible public datasets.
Apply for internships early and tailor applications to the role’s actual requirements.

blocks.text: The main goal is to demonstrate that you can do more than produce charts: you can transform data into accurate, well-supported decisions.
